entries.title: I Samuel 5:1
segments:
Ashdod; one of the cities of the Philistines. 
 
As a punishment to his people, God often suffers the wicked for a time to triumph over them, and to take from them many precious blessings.

entries.title: I Samuel 5:2
segments: Dagon; from dag, signifying a fish.  It was the name of an idol, the upper part of which was in the form of a man, and the lower part in that of a fish.

entries.title: I Samuel 5:4
segments:
Only the stump; in the original, the dagon, that is, the fishy part of the idol. 
 
All the efforts of the wicked to perpetuate their triumphs, and ultimately to prevail over the people of God, will be unavailing.

entries.title: I Samuel 5:5
segments: Tread on the threshold; from superstitious reverence towards it, as being the place where Dagon's body has lain.

entries.title: I Samuel 5:7
segments: God will finally convince all that they cnanot continue to oppose him and prosper, and that those things which they have idolized, and from which they expected help, have proved their ruin.

entries.title: I Samuel 5:8
segments:
Lords; rulers. 
 
  Gath; another city of the Philistines.

entries.title: I Samuel 5:9
segments: Emerods; hemorroids, or a species of the piles.

entries.title: I Samuel 5:10
segments:
Edkon; the northernmost city of the Philistines. 
 
All expedients of men to save themselves from the wrath of God, without returning in penitence and faith to him, are vain.

entries.title: I Samuel 5:11
segments: Very heavy; God smote them with sore judgments.

entries.title: I Samuel 5:12
segments: Diseases are God's servants; they go and come at his bidding, and all things in heaven, earth, and hell, are subject to his control.
